text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details, Mr. [Redacted]. Also, have you noticed any new moles or changes in existing ones elsewhere on your body?

text:
You have confirmed the lesion is growing, painless, and non-itchy; is it specifically shiny, translucent, or pearly in appearance, and do you see any small blood vessels (telangiectasias) or a central crater nearby? REQUEST TEST: Full body skin exam with dermoscopy of the chest lesion.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Full body skin exam with dermoscopy of the chest lesion: A single, partly elevated lesion located on the chest exhibiting asymmetry, border irregularity, varied color, and a diameter larger than 6mm. Palpation reveals the lesion is firm, partly elevated, and does not change form on pinching. Histopathology confirms atypical melanocytes infiltrating the epidermis and dermis, confirming the diagnosis of malignant melanoma. No shiny, translucent, or pearly appearance noted. No telangiectasias or central crater observed. No other new skin growths or changes noted elsewhere.
